account: Researchers from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre ran an individually randomized trial at diabetes and noncommunicable disease clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Between 8 March 2023 and 31 August 2024 they enrolled 2,378 adults with diabetes. In the AI group, retinal photographs went to the SELENA+ software from EyRIS, and each person received the result with face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room. In the standard group, people received a result from human graders by telephone a few weeks later. Among the 904 participants whom masked UK-certified graders judged to have referable diabetic retinopathy, 157 of 437 (35.9%) in the AI group attended the central ophthalmology clinic within eight weeks, against 85 of 467 (18.2%) in the standard group. The trial tests the whole pathway, so the effect combines the instant result with face-to-face counselling. Even in the AI group, nearly two in three people with referable disease did not attend within eight weeks. The British Council for the Prevention of Blindness, the Christian Blind Mission and the Sir Halley Stewart Trust funded the trial.
